_comment: Capital allocation, as its own object.
WHY NOT A FIELD ON THE PROJECT. It was one: `public_funding` on each row of
projects.json. That shape can only say what one project received, and the facts do not
arrange themselves that way — one Innovation Fund call finances several projects at
once, an IPCEI decision covers a consortium, and a state aid approval is a decision
about a country before it is a decision about a plant. A field on the recipient cannot
say any of that without repeating itself once per recipient, and repeated facts drift.
So funding is a node with edges out of it:
finances   -> project:      the money arrives here
supports   -> technology:   what it is being spent on
under      -> <file>:<id>   the legal basis, as a register measure
in         -> country:      where it lands
The project keeps a rollup, and the rollup is DERIVED — computed from these rows
wherever it is shown, never stored on the project. A stored total is a second copy of
a number, and a second copy is a number that will eventually disagree with the first.
STATUS IS NOT AMOUNT. `announced`, `approved`, `signed`, `disbursed` and `withdrawn`
are five different facts about the same euro figure, and a page that showed only the
figure would let a press release read as money in the ground. Everything here is
`approved`: a grant award or a government financing decision, stated by a party to it,
with no signature or disbursement reported in the document read.
`amount` names a parameter id rather than restating a number, so an amount cannot exist
here without the sentence it was read from existing in parameters.json. Where the
source states a programme but no figure, `amount` is null and `amount_note` says so —
an undisclosed amount and a zero are different states and this file distinguishes them.
`programme` is the measure id where the register carries the legal basis, and a named
string where it does not. Norway's Longship is the live case: it is a national decision
outside the register's perimeter, so it names itself and points at no measure.
WHAT THIS MODEL HOLDS, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT. Ruled 5 September 2026, after
the Innovation Fund retro-check turned two findings up that the file could not place.
IN: capital committed to BUILDING AN ADMITTED WORKS — a grant, a state aid approval, an
IPCEI decision or project finance whose recipient is a project on this platform and whose
purpose is the plant that project is. That is what the sector pages’ committed figure
means, and it is why the figure can be read as money going into the ground.
OUT: research and pilot funding. A framework-programme grant to a consortium testing a
process, or to a demonstration unit built to learn from rather than to produce, is money
spent on FINDING OUT rather than on building capacity, and the two do not add up. Summing
them would inflate every sector total by an amount that varies with how research-heavy
the industry is, which is the one thing a comparison between sectors must not do.
THE TWO FINDINGS THAT FORCED THE RULING, recorded here rather than landed as rows:
3D at Dunkirk holds about EUR 14.8 million of Horizon 2020 money for the DMX capture
pilot, and voestalpine’s H2Future at Linz about EUR 12 million for the electrolyser
demonstration. Both are real, both are traceable, and both are excluded by the boundary
above rather than by an oversight. Neither project loses its funding: 3D and H2Future are
pilots on this platform and their research money is a fact about them, which is why the
ROADMAP carries an entry for a research-funding layer that could hold it separately
instead of quietly inside a figure about building.
WHERE THE LINE IS HARD. A demonstration unit at commercial scale that also produces is a
judgement call, and the judgement is made on what the money was FOR as the awarding
document states it, not on the unit’s size. Where the document will not say, the row
does not land and the reason is written down.
